t.1.50.1: The sacrifice of Soma, the sacrifice of Varuṇa, and the sacrifice of Prajāpati took place at Prayāga; such is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bhāratas, O son of Parikṣit. May there be well-being for us and for those dear to us.
t.1.50.2: Śakra's sacrifice is said to number a hundred, and likewise another, equal in number, a hundred indeed; so too is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of Bhāratas, O son of Parikṣit. May there be well-being for us, your dear ones.
t.1.50.3: As was the sacrifice of Yama and of Harimedhas, as was the sacrifice of King Rantideva, so is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bhāratas, O son of Parikṣit; may there be well-being for us and for our loved ones.
t.1.50.5: As was the sacrifice of Nṛga, and of Ajamīḍha, and as was the sacrifice of King Dāśarathi, so is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bhāratas, O son of Parikṣit; may there be well-being for us and for those dear to us.
t.1.50.4: As was the sacrifice of Gaya, and the sacrifice of King Śaśabindu, and likewise that of King Vaiśravaṇa, so is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bhāratas, O son of Parikṣit. May there be well-being for us, your dear ones.
t.1.50.6: We have heard that the sacrifice of King Yudhiṣṭhira the Ajamīḍha, son of a god, was renowned in heaven; so too is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of the Bhāratas, son of Parikṣit. May there be well-being for us and for those dear to us.
t.1.50.7: Like the sacrifice of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Satyavatī, at which he himself performed the rite, so is this sacrifice of yours, O foremost of Bhāratas, son of Parikṣit. May there be well-being for us, your dear ones!
t.1.50.10: The god Vibhāvasu, Citrabhānu, the great-souled one, Hiraṇyaretas, the all-consuming one whose path is black, blazing with flames that circle to the right, the eater of oblations, desires this offering of yours.
t.1.50.8: For these priests, with the splendour of the sun and of fire, sit here as though at the sacrifice of the slayer of Vṛtra. No knowledge remains for them to learn today, and a gift once given would in no way be lost from them.
t.1.50.9: There is no officiating priest in all the worlds equal to Dvaipāyana; of this I am certain. For his disciples roam the earth, all of them officiating priests skilled in their own rites.
t.1.50.11: Here in the world of the living there is no other king equal to you as a protector of the people, and I am ever glad at heart because of your steadfastness. Either you are the king, or Yama, the King of Dharma.
t.1.50.13: You are like Khaṭvāṅga, Nābhāga and Dilīpa, equal in might to Yayāti and Māndhātṛ; your splendor rivals the splendor of the sun, and, firm in your vows, you shine like Bhīṣma.
t.1.50.12: Just as Śakra himself, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is the protector here, so are you here the protector of the creatures in this world. You are esteemed by us, O lord of men, here in this world, and there is no master of the sacrifice other than you.
t.1.50.14: Like Vālmīki's is your calm and steadfast fortitude, and like Vasiṣṭha's is your restrained anger; your lordship, in my view, is equal to Indra's, and your splendor shines like Nārāyaṇa's.
t.1.50.16: You are equal to Dambhodbhava in strength, and like Rāma you are skilled in weapons and in missiles; you are equal in splendour to Aurva and Trita, and, like Bhagīratha, you are difficult to look upon.
t.1.50.15: Like Yama, you know the firm determination of dharma; like Kṛṣṇa, you are endowed with every virtue. Just as in splendor you are the dwelling of the Vasus, so you are the very treasury of sacrifices.
t.1.50.17: Thus praised, all of them were pleased: the king, the members of the assembly, the officiating priests, and the oblation-bearing Fire. Seeing the feelings revealed in their gestures, King Janamejaya then spoke.
